speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Access to the sea brought us opportunities, enabled our nation to thrive and allowed us to define our place in the world.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: But the sea which has served as our lifeblood could also pose a threat to our very existence.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our businesses along the coast, such as shipyards or ports that rely on having access to the sea, will be at risk of coastal flooding.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In fact, Singapore already experiences coastal flooding during spring tides today, resulting in some parts of East Coast Park and Pulau Ubin being flooded.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: If we do nothing, places, like Changi Beach Park or East Coast Park, could become memories of the past.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We must therefore embark on coastal protection against sea level rise, to protect our land, our people and our livelihoods.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In 2020, to prepare Singapore for this long-term endeavour, we amended the Public Utilities Act (PUA) to designate PUB, Singapore's national water agency, as our coastal protection agency.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Planning, design and construction of coastal protection takes time.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: I will go through the Bill in several parts.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: First, I will explain our approach to coastal protection and PUB's role as the national coastal protection agency.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Second, who should undertake responsibility for coastal protection.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Third, how PUB will ensure completion of Singapore's coastal protection.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Fourth, when coastal protection obligations for landowners will be imposed.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Sixth, related and miscellaneous amendments pertaining to PUB's functions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: First, on our approach to coastal protection and PUB's role as the national coastal protection agency.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The goal of coastal protection is to stop seawater from flooding our land.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will protect our assets and livelihoods and preserve the functionality of the land.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To do so, we will need to establish a continuous line of defence that will protect against permanent coastal flooding caused by sea level rise, as well as transient coastal flooding from high tides and storm surges.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill will provide PUB with the powers to determine the location of this continuous line of defence and gazette this line as an Absolute Protection Boundary.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: PUB will decide where the Absolute Protection Boundaries are after carrying out studies on the different regions of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, we may want to allow for transient coastal flooding in some places.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There are some areas where access to the sea should be retained, such as beaches and coastal parks.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will therefore gazette Protection Boundaries to delineate the boundaries behind which the land must be protected from permanent coastal flooding.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In relation to these Boundaries, the Bill sets out four categories of Prescribed Places, which would have corresponding requirements of coastal protection measures to be put in place.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The first category comprises Prescribed Places at the Absolute Protection Boundaries.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These will need to be protected against permanent and transient coastal flooding.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The second category will comprise Prescribed Places bound by two boundary lines, the Absolute Protection Boundary on the landward side of the area, and Protection Boundary on the seaward side.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These places are known as "Transiently Floodable Areas (Coastal)".

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These need not be protected against permanent flooding but need to be protected against transient coastal flooding.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The third and fourth categories of Prescribed Places are Sheltered Structures within transiently floodable areas, such as food and beverage (F&B) venues as well as nearshore and offshore structures, like boardwalks and jetties.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Where these structures need to be functional at all times, they would need to be protected against permanent and transient coastal flooding.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: That said, exemptions can be sought if these structures can be allowed to flood transiently.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Not every existing land plot by the coast will be a Prescribed Place.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, PUB has adopted the "Long Island" project for City-East Coast under which the Absolute Protection Boundary will be located on new reclaimed land and the adjoining tidal gates that will be built.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Another example is the Greater Southern Waterfront which will have coastal barriers installed across the entrances of Keppel Harbour and Cruise Bay, to protect the land areas encircled by them.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The residential and commercial areas along HarbourFront and Keppel Bay, as protected by these coastal barriers, will therefore not be Prescribed Places.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill provides for coastal protection responsibilities to be undertaken by owners of Prescribed Places, or "landowners" for short.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is our current practice for coastal management.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Today, landowners along the coast already protect their buildings and infrastructure against coastal erosion.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: From time to time, they top up the crest level or repair their coastal structures although they do so without direction from PUB and do not necessarily join the coastal structures up with their neighbours'.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We believe that this approach of decentralising the responsibility of implementing coastal protection measures will achieve a solution that will work for the owner and achieve the public good of coastal protection.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our land is scarce, and we should optimise it where possible.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Therefore, we want to provide landowners the flexibility to select coastal protection measures that best meet their land use and waterfront needs.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will also avoid extensive reallocation or acquisition of land at the national level by the Government, which could potentially sterilise the valuable coastal land that we have.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: All landowners within the same region will have to complete their measures by the date to accord protection to all within the region.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These owners include the Government, Statutory Boards, as well as lessees with leases longer than three years.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As we engaged stakeholders, indeed, it became clear to us that different landowners require customised coastal protection measures to suit their individual needs.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The measures differ because of their unique land use and operational requirements.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For instance, for a shipyard with a dry dock, he may choose to build a seawall along the perimeter of the dry dock except the seaward entrance.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Landowners may also have preferred timelines to carry out their construction work.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It would not be practical, nor desirable, for the Government to implement standard coastal protection measures for such a wide range of land uses, from ports, ship building yards to petrochemical plants.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have engaged the vast majority of affected landowners prior to tabling this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: During our engagements with them, some shared that they had not factored the cost for additional coastal protection measures when the land was leased or purchased.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have considered their views and will be supporting landowners to fulfil their obligations through a few ways.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The grant will be sized according to cost norms, considering prevailing market rates and inflation.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Landowners can apply for the capital grant after the legal obligation to implement measures has been formally imposed on them.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The total grant amount will be split into reimbursement tranches to help with landowners’ planning and cashflow.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will further develop the grant details and share more information when ready.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Second, we will offer technical advice and consultations to landowners.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: At the same time, we have been levelling up industry competency on coastal protection through training programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will ensure that the local engineering industry has the proficiency to provide professional services to landowners to take on these projects and implement the measures to the standard required by PUB.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: While coastal protection works are undertaken by individual landowners, PUB will coordinate the works around the entire island, so that we can safeguard the long-term functionality of these coastal protection measures.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To keep seawater out, coastal protection measures need to be connected to each other, and the connection must be water-tight.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It also details how the responsibility of performing the connection will be allocated.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Where necessary, section 30P allows PUB to require neighbours to permit entry to their premises or render assistance, for the purposes of connecting the coastal protection measures.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: PUB will maintain centralised control and oversight of coastal protection through sections 30F and 30H.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Landowners will be required to seek PUB’s approval before undertaking coastal protection works, or before altering existing coastal protection measures.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Similar to other utility corridors, works within a designated coastal protection safety corridor, or Safety Corridor for short, will be regulated under the new section 30N.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The coastal protection measures and the Safety Corridor will be delineated in the Coastal Protection Interpretation Plan, or Interpretation Plan, under section 30C.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will be hosted on digital systems accessible to the public, where relevant details of coastal protection measures, and the locations of the Safety Corridor will be available.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Section 30I requires landowners to maintain, repair, inspect and monitor their measures.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Under section 30O, it will be an offence to damage the measures.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Should there be any observed damage to the measures, landowners will be required under section 30J to inform PUB and submit a rectification plan.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For landowners with deployable barriers, section 30K states that regulations may require these landowners to deploy the barriers before an imminent coastal flooding event, as required by PUB.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: PUB will develop forecasting abilities to anticipate potential coastal floods, so that early warning can be provided to landowners in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As I explained earlier, we will publish the locations of the Absolute Protection Boundaries and Protection Boundaries for each region after our studies are completed.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will do so when we have a clearer plan on the recommended coastal protection measures of the region.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: PUB will send out a First Notification to them after it has identified the indicative location of the continuous line of defence.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Second Notification will follow later to inform them of the specific coastal protection requirements, and the date by which the coastal protection measures must be in place.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will support landowners in fulfilling their obligations by publishing a Coastal Protection Code of Practice, or “the Code” for short.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: PUB aims to do so later this year, ahead of issuing the First Notifications.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will guide landowners and the industry on how to fulfil their coastal protection obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Landowners will have the flexibility to design the coastal protection measures around their needs, as long as they comply with the requirements stipulated in the Code.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As climate science continues to evolve, we will strike a balance between having protection early and overcommitting resources.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will want to have agility and flexibility in our coastal protection plans so that solutions can be adaptive to advancing climate projections and engineering solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The fifth group of amendments will confer powers to enable PUB to carry out its coastal protection functions, deter undesirable behaviours and provide immunities for officers to carry out their duties.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There will be penalties for actions that affect the continuous line of defence, and for failure to comply with a written notice from PUB.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our guiding principle for penalties is to ensure they are comparable to similar offences within the current SDA and other Acts.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Bill will amend section 43 of the SDA to provide PUB with emergency powers of entry, if, for example, the continuous line of defence is not yet complete due to delays, or a landowner cannot be contacted to deploy the coastal protection measure.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is especially important when an imminent coastal flooding event is forecasted.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As a last resort, PUB may also use the power of forced entry to enter the premises to address the coastal flood risk.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This power of forced entry will only be used judiciously, and only where there is an imminent coastal flooding event.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Similar to other Acts, to aid enforcement, the Bill will provide authorised officers with immunities under section 71 of the SDCPA so that they can confidently carry out their duties.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For the immunities to apply, authorised officers need to have acted in good faith and with reasonable care in the course of their actions.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: There are also amendments to reflect the intended scope of Subsidiary Legislation on the Waterborne Tax and the Water Conservation Tax, and to regulate activities in reservoirs and waterways.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have engaged the public and will continue to do so as we work on our coastal protection plans.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Through Our Coastal Conversations, PUB’s flagship dialogue for coastal protection, we have engaged the community, including residents, business owners, recreational and nature groups, on what they hope to see at our coastlines and what they value about our coastal spaces.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Even as PUB coordinates the overall approach for coastal protection, we will work with landowners and support them in fulfilling their obligations.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Today, as we stand on the firm foundations laid by our pioneers, so too must we build the safeguards of tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: By laying a strong foundation for coastal protection, we ensure that future generations inherit a resilient and liveable Singapore, on which they can build their dreams for an even better and prosperous Singapore.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: For weeks, my teammates and I were flying our helicopters to and fro along the coastline between Aceh and Meulaboh, distributing food, water and medical supplies to the survivors, as part of Singapore's humanitarian disaster relief efforts.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Until today, I can still remember vividly the sight of the massive scale of death and destruction along the coast of Sumatra.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: We were helping those who survived but we also witnessed first-hand the final journeys of others who did not.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: The tsunami was a black swan event that no one had predicted.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: But had there been seawalls built along the coastline, the scale and impact of destruction may have been mitigated.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: We must do all we can to protect our homes, our beaches, our parks and our factories from tidal waves and rising sea levels.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Hence, I agree with the objectives outlined in this Coastal Protection Bill.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: In response to this Bill, together with fellow People's Action Party (PAP) Members Nadia Samdin, Valerie Lee, Hany Soh, Lee Hui Ying as well as Cassandra Lee, we will cover concerns related to the integrity of water-tightness, clarity of Government funding, technical support from PUB, nature-based design solutions, impact on business operations, coordination between neighbouring companies, impact on land valuation as well as information asymmetry, defects and liability upon landownership change.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: On the other hand, the effectiveness of the coastal protection code of practice lies in the water-tightness of adjacent coastal protection measures so as to ensure a continuous line of protection against tidal waves and rising sea levels.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: The Coastal Protection Bill requires respective landowners to own, implement, maintain and operate coastal protection measures on their land premises.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: The purported rationale for placing the onus on landowners – no pun intended – is because landowners understand their sites best and thus have the flexibility to select measures that best suit their needs.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: They can even dovetail their infrastructure design and development with coastal protection works.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: As mentioned, the crux of the water-tightness of this continuous coastal protection measures lies in the integrity of the adjoining sections between two sections of seawalls or coastal protection measures.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: If the design and construction of individual coastal protection measure are not well-coordinated and constructed – and there could potentially be up to 100 such potential points of weakness – how can PUB ensure that when the high seas hit our shores one day, the collective assembly of multiple sections of differently designed measures can indeed withstand the forces of nature?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: I do not say this in anticipation of the shirking of individual responsibility.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Even if everyone plays his or her part, even if all 100 companies or landowners have the best of intentions, they may have knowledge gaps and coordination failures.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: How can we have an integrated and cohesive approach?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: An alternative model would be for PUB to undertake the design and construction for all stretches of vulnerable coastal areas, both Government and privately owned land.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: The Bill would provide PUB the authority to access the site, coordinate with landowners and construct the required coastal protection measures.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: After the coastal protection measures have been constructed, the ownership will then be novated to the landowner.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: The long-term responsibility of maintenance and operations will also rest with the landowners.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: After all, the Government, as the largest landowner of coastlines, will be responsible for implementing coastal protection for majority of coastlines.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: The cost of construction for all coastal protection measures could be recovered from this fund.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: This also allows us to leverage economies of scale, working with qualified consultants and construction companies that have a good track record and quality of work.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: If the protection measures are well designed and well constructed from day one, the long-term maintenance will also be less onerous and better maintained.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: To be clear, the crux is this – the responsibility is private, but the good is public.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: We may have 100 possible points of failure.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Even one point of failure can cause massive damage.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: Our strongest remedy, our best hope, lies in one coordinating power.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang West)
text: That way, our little island-nation can be truly well protected against the tidal waves during extreme weather and rising sea levels for the long run.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: As a low-lying nation, we cannot afford to wait.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: However, as we move from planning to legislation, we must ensure that the continuous line of defence we build is not merely an engineering success, but one that is socially and fiscally responsible.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Our legislative framework must also be robust enough to manage the complexities of land tenure, private sector compliance and the preservation of our national identity.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Private owners and lessees who hold the remaining sections will need to implement their own coastal protection measures.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Under the proposed legislation, private landowners and lessees are responsible for installing and upholding coastal protection structures.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: It appears that landowners have the autonomy to choose protection strategies that align with their specific requirements and conditions, enabling them to integrate coastal defence works into their existing and future development schedules, ensuring both flexibility and efficiency in implementation.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I would also like to ask the Minister to give us an indication of, among the non-state entities-related owners or lessees, the number or ratio of the non-Government entities or non-Government-linked corporations who are owners and lessees, be they individuals, Management Corporations Strata Title (MCSTs), clubs or other non-business or non-state entities.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I also like to ask whether there are any industrial lessees who may have shorter remaining tenures from now, for example, less than 10 years.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If so, how many of such companies are we looking at?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Can the Government elaborate with some detail the financial support, that is, the grant details as well as the technical support it is giving under the new law, including the level of support?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: How would the packages work for multinational companies (MNCs) as well as small and medium sized companies (SMEs)?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Equally, how do we ensure that the non-commercial entities are adequately supported under this Bill?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Will there be tiered subsidies, specifically for local SMEs who may lack the cash reserve for major Government-linked Corporations and MNCs?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Will the financial support mentioned be a one-off grant at the onset or will it help SMEs and MCSTs cover the recurring costs of specialised maintenance?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Further, will the Minister also consider a framework where lease extensions are tied to coastal protection investments?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We must ensure that a continuous line does not suffer from fragmented tenures.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: What happens if a lessee fails to complete construction before giving up the lease?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: If a waterfront company runs into financial problems or go into liquidation and is not able to build or to complete the construction, we may also be left with a public safety risk that neighbours cannot fix alone.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: How will the Government intervene in such a situation?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Separately, will the Government require performance bonds from private lessees to ensure funds are available to complete the project if the state or another state-appointed entity is required to complete the works required?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Further, how will liability be transferred if a plot is returned to the state midway through the 10-year notice period?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: How would the Government supervise and ensure timely construction commence and completion within the 10-year period?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Is the Government considering implementing mandatory construction milestones?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Does the PUB have step-in rights to take over any lagging project and charge the cost back to the owner before the 10-year window expires?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Would there be onsite supervision by PUB to ensure project milestone completion?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: How do we ensure that lessees account for their lack of action or delay?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: This will also ensure that the contractor or contractors appointed will have the right expertise, experience, common understanding of each area and also economies of scale for the lessees, for the landowners.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: While this code will provide the technical blueprint for our defences, we must ensure that these structures can complement and even enhance our natural environment and heritage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Will the Government consider requiring the Code of Practice to mandate a nature-first visibility assessment before landowners are permitted to resort to traditional concrete seawalls?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Even as I expect many of the current sites affected by the Bill may already be in use for industrial and commercial purposes, if there are segments containing any significant heritage value, the Government should have appropriate heritage assessment mechanisms to decide how any such historical markers can be suitably preserved and protected.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: For greater transparency on fund usage and decision-making, I hope the Government will consider tabling an annual coastal resilience report detailing Coastal and Flood Protection Fund disbursements and progress across both public and private sectors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: What is the public-private split in the expenditure?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the principles of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Given that the sea wall construction is expensive, I am concerned about whether these businesses can obtain sufficient support to ensure that their operations are not negatively affected.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: At the same time, I am also concerned about how to avoid businesses pulling out early due to unviable investments, thereby leaving gaps in our line of defence.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I am concerned with the upcoming Coastal Protection Code of Practice – how it will balance the hard engineering standards with ecological protection.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope that the Code will adopt nature-based solutions, such as mangroves and adopt designs for transient floodable areas, ensuring that while strengthening coastal defences, the public can still continue to enjoy precious waterfront spaces.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Although I have the above concerns, I support this Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I hope that through strict supervision, we can protect our coastline and also the long-term interests of all Singaporeans. : In conclusion, Mr Deputy Speaker, climate adaptation is a marathon that requires every stakeholder to stay the course.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: We must ensure our framework can withstand economic fluctuations and business exits over time.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: By implementing tighter supervision and clearer financial safeguards now, we protect not just our coastlines but the long-term interest of all Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Coastal protection measures will only become increasingly relevant and critical.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To me, the purport of this Bill hits the nail on the head.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I therefore raise several clarifications to the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These are the specific stakeholders whose concerns and feedback must be heard.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For the practicality of this Bill's proposals and our coastal protection plan ought to be guided by the said group.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is not confined to the effectiveness of the Coastal Protection Measures but also and, perhaps, more importantly, the administrations of the Code of Practice and grants, which will all go towards the success or failure of the policy's objectives.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If so, how does PUB intend to ensure that the responsibility does not fall through the cracks when there is a transition in ownership or occupation by a lessor?

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Our identity as a nation is inseparable from identity as an island.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We were a small coastal settlement before we were a colony and a natural harbour before we were a nation.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Singapore River was what made us prosperous and the Straits of Malacca made us globally relevant.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is the whole story, and it is not unique to us either.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Wherever human beings have built something lasting, they have built it near water.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And today, 40% of the world's population stays within 100 kilometres of a coast.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The world's most beloved cities – Shanghai, New York, Barcelona, our own Marina Bay – they sit at the meeting point of land and water.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This Bill is protecting the relationship between us, our island and the sea that made it.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, we are legislating right now for the people who will live in that world.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And that is the reason I want to speak today, about what we are defending for and what we can become in the act of defending it.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I want to make two arguments: one, that how we design our coastal defences matters as much as whether we build them; and two, that what Singapore builds here has the potential to serve not just our own shores but the shores of nations across our region and in doing so, build a new pillar of Singapore's economy.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The conventional framing of coastal defence is adversarial – water is the threat, infrastructure is the shield, we build the wall, we hold the line and we keep the sea at bay.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But this Bill already contains the seed of a different philosophy.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It introduces concept of the transiently floodable area, a coastal zone designed to accept water periodically, rather than resist it permanently, it opens the door to designing with water rather than purely against it.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, my question to the Minister is about execution.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Code of Practice merely dictate technical details, like the height of sea walls and the specifications of pumps, or will it actively incentivise developers and landowners to think about what these spaces could be for the 99% of the time that they are dry?

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A transiently floodable area that is well designed becomes a park, a waterfront promenade, a community space.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: One that is not well designed becomes a fenced-off eyesore.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And which Singapore do we want to build?

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some of the world's most admired cities already have shown what designing with water looks like in practice.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Rotterdam has water squares, which are sunken public plazas that fill during heavy rain and function as parks and markets the rest of the time.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Copenhagen has redesigned entire boulevards to channel floodwater while remaining fully functional streets.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They are celebrated urban transformations; places people actively want to be that also happen to function as flood management systems.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singapore also already knows how to do this.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Marina Bay is simultaneously a reservoir, a tidal barrier and one of the most iconic public spaces in Asia.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We did not choose between flood defence and urban liveability.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The "Long Island" project off the East Coast, with 20 kilometres of new waterfront, is an opportunity on the same scale.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What I would ask is that the design case be made with equal ambition.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Not just how do we protect this land from the sea, but what kind of coastline do we want future Singaporeans to inherit.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Designing with water does not prescribe a single solution.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is a broad philosophy that can encompass built solutions, hybrid structures or nature-based solutions.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But the last category, nature-based solutions, deserve special mention because of the scientific case for it being so strong.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Coral reef restoration costs roughly one-fifteenth the per metre cost of artificial breakwaters.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singapore's own 100k Corals Initiative, launched in December of 2024, is already integrating living reefs into our coastal protection strategy.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Nature-based solutions are, in many cases, superior to hard engineering – on cost, on performance and on liveability.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I would ask the Minister to let the Code of Practice embed an active design philosophy, one that goes beyond technical standards to incentivise integrated water-positive solutions, especially nature-based ones.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are building legal frameworks, engineering standards, a digital Coastal Protection Interpretation Plan and a technical Code of Practice.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are adapting polar technology for tropical conditions at Pulau Tekong.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are generating what the Centre for Climate Research Singapore describes as the world's highest resolution climate projections for Southeast Asia.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are doing all of this on a tropical island in an equatorial climate surrounded by the ecosystems – mangroves, coral reefs, tropical peat coastlines – that define coastal defence in this part of the world.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: No one else is doing this at this scale in this geography.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: That matters because the countries that need coastal resilience expertise most urgently are not the Dutch.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Jakarta alone has 40% of its land below sea level, with some districts sinking at 180 millimetres a year.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These nations need solutions, and the dominant global expertise in coastal protection, the Dutch model, built over centuries, was designed for temperate conditions, for clay soils and North Sea storm surges.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Not for tropical peat that subsides at five centimetres per year, not for monsoon hydrology and compound flooding and not for the mangroves and coral reefs that must be both engineered and ecologically sustained.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Researchers have documented what they call the impasse in transferring Dutch delta plans to Jakarta.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The soils, the institutions and the ecological conditions are simply too different.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Dutch water export sector generates nearly €10 billion annually.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Bangladesh Delta Plan, the Mekong Delta Plan and the rebuilding of the City of New Orleans after Hurricane Katrina, Dutch expertise sits at the centre of all of them.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They turn centuries of national need into a global industry, and that is a model worth studying and emulating.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Singapore is positioned to do for the tropics what the Dutch did for the temperate world.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have the research infrastructure – the Earth Observatory of Singapore, the Tropical Marine Science Institute, the Centre for Climate Research Singapore – and we have the training networks.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We host the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre and we lead on green finance through the Singapore-Asia Taxonomy and we now have, through this Bill, a legal and regulatory framework for tropical coastal protection being built from first principles.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The intellectual property being developed through this programme, the engineering standards, the legal frameworks and the climate models represent enormous potential value.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And there is an additional dimension beyond commerce.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The SIJORI Growth Triangle – Singapore, Johor, Riau – is deeply integrated with our economy and our workforce and our daily life.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Flood risk in these communities is not an abstract concern for us.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Helping our immediate neighbours build resilience is straightforward in Singapore's interest.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A Singapore that exports coastal resilient expertise is not being just generous; it is being strategic.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Every generation of Singaporeans has wagered on this island's future.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The founding generation wagered that city with no hinterland could become a nation.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The generation that built our water infrastructure wagered that necessity could become self-sufficiency.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The generation now in Parliament is being asked to protect this island and the relationship with the water that made us for the generations that follow.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe we can do more than just protect what we have.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We want future Singaporeans to look back at this moment and see a generation that designed with the water, shared what it learnt and left a coastline more alive than the one it inherited.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We are not the owners of this coastline, we are its stewards, and future generations will judge whether we kept it well.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: The impact of the rising sea levels from climate change is significant.

speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
text: I support the Bill as it recognises the longer-term challenge that Singapore faces.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This is higher than more than 30% of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Smaller island-nations, such as Tuvalu and Kiribati have had to make plans for relocation of their population.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: We are fortunate and lucky to be larger.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: But fail to plan, plan to fail – our future generations may one day face the prospect of having to leave our island.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: I thus support this Bill as it makes the preparations we need to stay on the map, even into the next century.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First, our coastal protection requires us to build a continuous line of defence.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Each may take a different approach to comply with the Bill.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Responsible landowners would invest heavily in constructing their coastal defences, but some may choose to minimise costs, especially if they are on a temporary lease.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Code of conduct provide sufficient guidance to promote consistent implementation between landowners?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Or will PUB act as an overall coordinator to pre-approve coastal defence plans?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Would it be more efficient for the Government to build maybe the entire coastal defence line and then seek reimbursement from landowners?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: The Bill makes reference to implementing coastal management via nature-based solutions.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This is ideal as nature-based solutions bring added benefits, such as preserving biodiversity and reducing emissions.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: How will we encourage landowners to adopt nature-based solutions?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: These could be more difficult to set up and integrate in a continuous defence line.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Will there be technical guidance to help them integrate nature-based solutions with other coastal management features?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Second, how will we manage the smooth implementation of this Bill over such a long timeframe?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Over 10 years, and surely by the year 2100, we can expect that landowners, lessees and personnel have gone through various changes.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Effective handover of knowledge is crucial for these measures to be effective.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Will PUB set guidelines or conditions for the handover of technical knowledge to new landowners or lessees to preserve critical technical knowledge of privately-built coastal defences during transitions?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Can critical data be centrally stored in the Coastal Protection Interpretation Plan, so that new owners, or even the Government, can step in where needed?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: It is also important to stay accountable and be accountable for financial support that we provide over such a long period.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: How will the use of the grants be tracked over this period to ensure funds are properly deployed to coastal protection?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: What happens if landowners receive the grant and then liquidate or sell the property during the 10-year term?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, we must strike a difficult balance between building resilience for the future and succeeding in the present.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Coastal landowners are those in key strategic sectors, such as shipping and energy.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore's future also requires that they can stay competitive in the global economy.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Constructing and maintaining coastal protections is a costly responsibility.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: In-depth studies and top-quality workmanship are needed to build effective defences.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: After construction, the coastal defences also need constant maintenance from sea erosion damage.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Like the seas, businesses have its high and low tides.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Do we have contingency plans in place to provide support?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Otherwise, we might not only have poorly maintained structures, but possibly lose valuable businesses.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   As a small-island nation, rising sea levels pose a real threat to Singapore.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: By 2100, sea levels are projected to rise to 1.15 metres, and during extreme weather, could even surge to five metres.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This is already higher than over 30% of Singapore's land.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Some smaller island-nations have already had to plan to relocate their citizens.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: If we do not plan early, our descendants may one day also face a situation of having to leave this island.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: There are three things that I would like to raise.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: First, our coastal protection needs to establish a continuous line of defence.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: This implementation process must remain consistent and highly integrated.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Second, how do we ensure that this Bill can be smoothly implemented over such a long period of time?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Financial support over such a long duration also needs to ensure there is proper accountability.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: How can we track the use of funding during this period to ensure that funds are properly used for coastal protection?

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Building and maintaining coastal protection facilities is an expensive responsibility.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: Once built, these facilities will still need maintenance to cope with erosive damages from sea water.

speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying (Nee Soon)
text: When coastal landowners face difficult market conditions or short-term cash flow challenges, how should maintenance work continue? : Sir, notwithstanding my clarifications, I stand in support for the smooth sailing implementation of this Bill.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Speaker, as an island-nation, the sea has always shaped our geography, our history, it will also shape our future.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Today, as we debate the Coastal Protection Bill, we recognise a simple truth: rising sea levels and intensifying weather patterns are no longer distant projections, but real risks that require serious and long-term action.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: But our shorelines are not empty edges of the land.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: They host critical infrastructures and industries, keeping our nation alive economically and quite literally, including ports, petrochemical facilities, aviation infrastructure, logistics hubs and energy installations.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: These coastal areas are part of our arteries and veins, sustaining us in our part of the world.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: And they provide thousands of jobs for our Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I am sure we can all agree that coastal protection is necessary.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: The question before us is not whether we protect our coastlines, but how we ensure that implementation is effective, coordinated and sustainable over the long term.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: As we move forward, it is therefore important that we consider how responsibilities and resources are allocated between the state, industries that operate along the coast and future generations – in a way that remains fair and economically sound.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: With this, Speaker, I have a few clarifications to seek, centred around three themes: first, the scope of funding; second, implementation; and third, coordination efforts.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Notwithstanding, I understand that the Ministry intends to provide financial support in the form of a capital grant.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: While capital expenditure for the initial construction of coastal protection measures may be supported, coastal protection is not a one-time investment.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Over time, these measures will erode, require upgrades and incur ongoing operational and maintenance costs.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Will the Ministry consider whether support could extend to such incremental lifecycle costs, given that these measures ultimately contribute to national resilience?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: In addition, some coastal sites host critical national infrastructure, such as power generation facilities or maritime installations.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: In such cases, will funding support be coordinated across the relevant Ministries, so that coastal protection for these strategic assets can be approached as a whole-of-Government effort, rather than solely through the landowners' framework?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: They may include elevating land, implementing polder systems and constructing floodgates or seawalls.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Such works can involve substantial construction activity, including sheet piling, deep soil mixing and ground improvement works.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: For coastal industrial sites, these works may take place within or near operating critical infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: For instance, certain power generation facilities rely on seawater intake systems and are located close to the shoreline.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Construction activities in the vicinity may carry risks of operational disruption if not carefully coordinated.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: In this regard, may I ask whether the Ministry has considered how such risks will be managed?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Would the Minister agree that coordination with the relevant agencies should not be left solely to the affected businesses or landowners and a single point of contact will be useful.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Given the potential implications for essential services, a whole-of-Government coordination effort may be necessary, involving the relevant sectoral agencies alongside the implementing authorities.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Further, under the amendments to the Sewerage and Drainage Act, notifications will be issued to landowners.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Could the Minister clarify what level of detail these notices will contain?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: In the initial batch of notices, will they indicate only general areas where measures are required or will they provide more precise specifications?

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Greater clarity at that early stage would help stakeholders plan investments and align their implementation timelines more effectively.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: I would now like to ask about coordination between neighbouring landowners.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: While the intent of ensuring a continuous line of defence is very clear, implementation may not always be straightforward.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: In industrial clusters such as Jurong Island or Tuas, companies operate facilities with very different operational requirements and site configurations.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Left purely to neighbouring parties, coordination may become complex.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: Differences could arise over design choices, implementation timelines or cost allocation, and these issues may have knock-on effects on the integrity of the overall coastal defence line.

speaker: Ms Valerie Lee (Pasir Ris-Changi)
text: With these clarifications, Sir, I support the Bill and I look forward to the Minister's response.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As an island city-state, our proximity and access to the sea is an important part of our identity.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Along our shores are where many Singaporeans first learn to cycle, sail, fish, barbecue with family, dive or simply watch the sunset.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For me, the coast is also where my husband and I enjoy slowing down with my son when time permits – pointing out boats along our shores.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Our coasts also support a wide range of activities and livelihoods: from sustaining trade to aquaculture and the protection of coastal habitats, such as mangroves and coral reefs.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As climate change intensifies and Singapore strengthens coastal protection, these measures will inevitably shape our coastal environments and the people connected to them.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This Bill is an important step in ensuring that our shores remain safe, healthy and accessible for generations to come.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Coastal protection, however, is technically complex and I am heartened that the Ministry and PUB have developed a nuanced plan that recognises the differing needs of stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Naturally, their interests may be more site-specific than system-wide and there may arise situations where a landowner implements a more modest measure, whereas integrated coastal defence requires more comprehensive works.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In some parts of the world, coastal protection has successfully taken on an integrated approach that can attenuate wave energy, enhance biodiversity and in some cases even create usable public spaces alongside protection works.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, sponge cities in Denmark and China or living shorelines in America.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Beyond individual sites, coastal protection also operates as a connected system which the Minister has emphasised.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Bill rightly requires continuity along the adjacent land parcels.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Ministry please elaborate how PUB will support the coordination, so that the overall coastal system functions cohesively?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the event there are differing timelines or approaches adopted by the neighbouring landowners, what mechanisms will PUB have to step in and ensure timely alignment so that gaps do not emerge so as to avoid implementation risks?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This need for continuity also extends over time beyond the parcels, as land ownership may change.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Bill allows for up to 10 years for owners to implement measures, which is helpful for long-term planning and coordination.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, there may be instances where land ownership changes during this period.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Could the Ministry clarify how continuity of planning and coordination with new owners will be ensured if and when coastal land changes ownership after the protection requirements or boundaries have been designated?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Has the Ministry considered how many such parcels have changed hands over the past 10 or 20 years?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given these coordination and implementation complexities, support for landowners will be important.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I therefore appreciate the technical expertise, planning coordination and financial assistance the Government will provide.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We inherited a coastline shaped with foresight, and it is our responsibility now to safeguard the shores that support livelihoods, leisure and our connection to the sea.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In doing so, we ensure that future generations will continue to know Singapore not only as a global city, but also as an island home that will endure and thrive in the face of climate change. :   Waves roll by the shore, Sea breeze greets the morning light, Coastlines guarded more and more, For future generations' sight. : Thank you, Sir.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Many Members have given very good suggestions, have been very encouraging, I would say.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Some even calling the Bill a strategic one, not just for the protection of Singapore's coastline but also as a new area of growth, new possibilities of jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, we are very hopeful that coastal protection will be an area where Singapore, being a frontrunner, will be able to accumulate the expertise and experience that can then be useful to other countries and other cities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Allow me to run through the queries and concerns raised by Members, which I will address in five broad themes.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: First, on who should be responsible for coastal protection.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Poh Li San, Ms Hany Soh and Ms Lee Hui Ying asked if the Government should instead implement coastal protection on behalf of landowners, to maximise efficiency and coordination.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This will allow for the optimisation of the very scarce and precious land that we have.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having the Government centrally implement solutions will be sub-optimal, since it may not be feasible to account for every landowner's unique needs and timelines.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Landowners are most familiar with their sites and are better placed to implement coastal protection measures that best meet their business needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, in our engagements, landowners expressed concern on the potential disruptions when enacting the coastal protection measures and wanted flexibility to dovetail coastal protection works with their redevelopment plans and business cycles.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Centralised specialised measures, like the barriers we are proposing for the Greater Southern Waterfront or the reclaimed "Long Island", are also not always relevant to the land uses in the region nor cost effective.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That said, we will facilitate the process as much as possible.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: For the companies that lease industrial land from JTC, actually this is the vast majority of the private landowners, PUB is working closely with JTC to explore a centralised procurement model, as well as other options that can support JTC's lessees in fulfilling their coastal protection obligations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The responsibility for coastal protection will apply only to landowners of Prescribed Places.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will gazette the Absolute Protection Boundaries in Subsidiary Legislation and publish it in the Coastal Protection Interpretation Plan, which would be discoverable during legal conveyancing.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: These efforts would help address Ms Nadia Samdin's and Ms Hany Soh's as well Ms Poh Li San's points on ensuring that there is no information asymmetry and that coastal protection obligations do not fall through the cracks in the event of a change in land ownership.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In addition, ahead of the formal gazetting, PUB will work towards publishing the indicative locations of the Absolute Protection Boundaries and the Protection Boundaries in the public domain, so that prospective lessees and landowners will be aware of their potential obligations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Cassandra Lee also asked about liabilities and responsibilities arising from the transfer of land ownership.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Our principle is that landowners will be responsible for implementing and maintaining the coastal protection measures on their land.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When there is a transfer of ownership, the transfer of liability is no different from when property changes hands today.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In addition, the previous landowner would have had to engage a Qualified Person to certify that the structure is up to standard, before PUB approves it as a coastal protection measure.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Landowners would also have to regularly inspect and maintain any coastal protection measures they have, according to PUB's standards.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Cassandra Lee had questions on what happens if there are multiple owners, and what their respective obligations would be.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Under the new section 2D of the Bill, the Government will make clear in regulations whether the lessor or the lessee is considered for the relevant coastal protection obligations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the separate question of co-ownership, I would like to inform Ms Lee that we do not currently have any such cases.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: However, should this scenario arise, co-owners will each be responsible for coastal protection obligations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The second set of questions covers how PUB will play a coordinating role among landowners, especially when the coastal protection measures must join up to form this continuous line of defence.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying spoke about the importance of preserving critical knowledge of the coastal protection measures, as land may change hands.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will also keep records of the reports and drawings, and can require a transfer of the records to the incoming landowner when there is a change in land ownership.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Valerie Lee, Ms Nadia Samdin, Ms Poh Li San and Ms Lee Hui Ying asked about the challenges on the ground for landowners and how PUB would facilitate coordination so that measures are connected and water-tight.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Bill has provided for this coordination role.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Section 30G allows PUB to provide as-built drawings or plans of the neighbouring plot to a landowner, if necessary, to ensure that the connection is effected.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It will set out the baseline planning, design, operation and maintenance requirements for landowners' compliance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It will also spell out what landowners need to take note of when connecting their measures, such as designing for water-tightness.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Where necessary, PUB will use its enforcement powers to ensure the continuous line of defence is not compromised.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This includes the scenario that Ms Lee Hui Ying asked about, for companies who face short-term liquidity challenges and are unable to maintain their coastal protection measures, or even non-compliant landowners who fail to fulfil their coastal protection responsibilities.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: First, PUB has power under sections 41 and 44 to step in and undertake maintenance and repair works to ensure the functionality of the continuous line of defence and to recover the cost as necessary from the landowner subsequently.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Second, PUB has powers of forced entry, which we will use in the scenario when there is an imminent coastal flood, but the landowner does not have a fully implemented coastal protection measure in place and is unresponsive or uncontactable, notwithstanding efforts to contact them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When activating such powers of forced entry, PUB officers will be required to seek PUB senior management's approval before proceeding with forced entry into these premises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will do so to either activate a deployable measure or put in place an interim measure.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This would only be used as a last resort when the officers have exhausted all other available options, including the deployment of measures outside of the premises.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is vital for PUB to have the forced entry power in such a scenario, to join up the continuous line of defence and ensure public safety and protect assets.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Valerie Lee and Ms Nadia Samdin asked if maintenance of coastal protection measures will be funded through the grant.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are still working out the grant details, and more information will be released when ready.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The intent of the grant is to fund the necessary costs of putting in place the coastal protection measure.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We have assessed that the maintenance required of measures such as seawalls and revetments are minimal, and that this would not be substantially different from how landowners might maintain their existing seawalls and revetments today.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This would allow us to monitor the progress of works.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Should there be a change in landownership before the completion date, the new landowner has the option of using the previous set of plans or submitting a fresh set of plans to PUB for approval.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are ramping up efforts to prepare the local industry as we embark on coastal protection.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: There are two main groups here – the consultants and the construction contractors that will put in place the coastal protection measures and the flood protection managers that will assist the landowner with meeting the coastal protection requirements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: On the issue of capability building, Ms Cassanda Lee asked if we would consider developing a list of contractors that landowners can engage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I believe Mr Dennis Tan made the same point.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The coastal protection measures that landowners need to implement are unlikely to be significantly different from the seawalls, revetments or embankments that are seen in Singapore today.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are surrounded by sea and we have coastal protection measures today.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Coastal landowners would likely be familiar with contractors involved in such works.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: To Ms Nadia Samdin's point on how we will encourage landowners to take a long-term view during implementation, the Code of Practice will provide a set of minimum standards covering planning, design, operation and maintenance of coastal protection measures to ensure our continuous line of defence is sufficiently robust.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Landowners are also required to seek PUB's approval for their plans before construction.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, there is some quality checks on the part of PUB.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This is when PUB can assess if the measure is sufficiently designed while keeping the longer-term needs in mind.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In my opening speech, I have also explained that the Code and what we are planning will also be updated in time to come, because we are continuously, regularly refining our projections on sea level rise, on storm surges and also, at the same time, researching into new engineering solutions, new technology that can help us.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Code will not be something that is fixed in time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I am sure we will review and we will update it over time.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We agree with Ms Cassandra Lee on the importance of flood protection managers.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The intent of appointing flood protection managers is to have trained personnel who can assist landowners in fulfilling their coastal protection obligations such as inspecting and maintaining the measures.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The last group of questions relates to the impact to the environment.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
