text: Very important questions, and I am sure many groups of nature lovers as well as members of the public, local community groups will also be keen to know how the coastlines will be affected by coastal protection measures.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Indeed, we placed a lot of emphasis in upfront site studies, in engagement, in listening very closely, in discussing, in to and fro exchange of ideas with relevant groups so that we can come together to agree on a set of workable designs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: That is done at the site-specific study level.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will have to conform and work within the EIA framework.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Ms Lee Hui Ying and Ms Nadia Samdin, as well as Mr Andre Low, as well as Mr Dennis Tan, asked how we will encourage landowners to adopt nature-based solutions or to maintain some of their heritage value and whether there will be any technical guidance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: During our site-specific studies, we engage the community and nature groups to determine the location of the measures to preserve and encourage biodiversity where possible, including, for example, whether the continuous line of defence can be set behind mangroves to minimise the impact to them.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This was done as part of PUB's "Coastal Conversations" for the Sungei Buloh area, for example.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, my point is, the consideration for the environment, for the conservation of nature and the protection of biodiversity is done at the site study stage.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: When that is done, after consulting all relevant stakeholders, after arriving at the solution that we think is optimal, that itself will be developed into detailed requirements for the prescribed places, to be in the interpretation plan and to be gazetted.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: So, by the time that the landowner receives specific requirements in their second notification, the consideration is already done.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We would have moved back from protected area.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The line would have been drawn behind and therefore, impacting the owners.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: What the owners could do will be limited as far as environmental protection and consideration is concerned, although there are some considerations when it comes to using environmentally friendly, hybrid solutions, which over time, we hope to include in our Code of Practice that the landowners can then include in their specific sites.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This Bill does not dictate the site-specific study process.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Landowners have the flexibility to determine the coastal protection measures that best meet their land needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As part of the Coastal Protection and Flood Management Research Programme, there is ongoing research to assess the efficacy of hybrid nature-based solutions for coastal protection.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Where applicable, these nature-based solutions will be shared in future editions of the Code of Practice.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: I would just like to also repeat what Senior Parliamentary Secretary Goh Hanyan had said in the Committee of Supply, that we are going to publish a guidebook that is called the Flood Resilient Developments Guidebook, that is developed through an Alliance for Action on how we can incorporate some of these design elements.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: This guide will allow the landowners to have a collection of references that may be easier for them to consider as they carry out their works.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: (In Mandarin):   Coastal protection is crucial as it affects our daily lives and safety.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Coastal Protection Bill will help Singapore establish a continuous line of defence along coastal areas to resist threats from rising sea levels, protecting our people, assets and livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: After the Bill is passed, landowners can choose measures that adapt to local conditions and adopt appropriate coastal protection measures according to their organisational needs.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: PUB will also ensure that coastal protection measures of adjoining sections can be properly connected.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We will engage landowners and coordinate among them to ensure that they work closely together to adopt appropriate measures.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We appreciate all the suggestions made by our Members on how to better support the landowners.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The collective efforts currently made by coastal landowners for protection of the coast will lay a solid foundation for our country's coastal protection and benefit future generations.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: The Government will work together with the people to address rising sea levels due to climate change, implement long-term coastal protection measures and jointly build a more resilient, safe and prosperous Singapore. : Mr Speaker, coastal protection is a long-term endeavour to protect our people, assets and livelihoods.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Coastal protection is not a burden that reduces business competitiveness.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Rather, it is an investment to ensure business continuity in a world where climate risks will become more apparent.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: First one, in clause 30G, it was mentioned that the new section in this clause provides for the owner the obligation for connecting the coastal protection measure for its prescribed place, to the coastal protection measure for an adjacent prescribed place.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: As highlighted earlier in my speech, the crux of the problem is really the water tightness of the protection measure.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: In the event of a compromised measure due to the failure at the interface, would there then be a penalty meted out to the original landowner or on his neighbour?

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: The second one is, Minister also mentioned that penalties will be metered out to landowners who compromise the continuous coastline of defence.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: PUB will force-enter or take over the works, especially in the event of imminent flooding events.

speaker: Ms Poh Li San
text: My question is, if it is something that is quite an extreme weather, like a tidal wave that is expected to hit in the next hour or so, will PUB then be able to respond in time, put in some kind of temporary barriers?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Of course, we will have to look at the facts of the case, whether it is due to the design or an implementation error, or is it due to maintenance errors.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If I were to put in principle, we are looking at responsible decisions made by the landowner.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: What we have in mind is not activate this preparedness or this preparation an hour before a flood arrives.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are investing a lot into the ability to forecast.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And we hope that we are able to forecast days in advance.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: If we have days in advance, we could go around to look at areas where we can give advance notice to owners.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Landowners could then put up some of their temporary or some of their defence.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: I have just two points, mainly related to the site-specific studies, as it appears that this is a very key part of the process, and I am not sure if I missed it.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: First, in the event there are differing timelines or approaches adopted by neighbouring landowners, given that each measure will really depend on the site, what is the formal mechanism that PUB has to step in and ensure that there is alignment across implementation?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: The second is, how will interested groups and members of the public be made aware about the timing of these site-specific studies and is there any opportunities for citizen scientists to get involved?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Because I appreciate the Minister's assurances that nature will be well considered and integrated, but for nature-based solutions, these have to be very intentionally designed and woven in as part of the process.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We place a lot of emphasis on engaging the community, the local community.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Earlier on, Ms Cassandra Lee talked about how businesses in her constituency have been consulted – that is really a reflection of the amount of effort and work that PUB colleagues have put in to reach out, to contact and to meet up and to have deep discussions about the obligations and the options.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Similarly, we have done so as we move from region to region, conducting site-specific studies, engaging local community, local businesses as well as nature groups, different nature groups, from those that are interested in plant materials to those who are interested in corals, we want to reach out as widely as possible.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Having done so over the last few years, I think we have created a good network among interested parties.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And the stakeholders, important stakeholders have come forward and participated fully in the process, moving from region to region, as we finish one, we move onto another one.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: At the same time, we have also moved back the boundary lines in some cases, allowing some transient flooding to occur at Sungei Buloh, really after having long discussions.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Because I think the nature groups, having done these extensive discussions with us for many sessions, going through the options deeply, they understand also.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Trade-offs have to be made, it is not an easy process, but we have done so already with many groups over several rounds, and we believe that we have come to a process that is useful for all parties, all parties – Government, people, users, sports users, recreation users, environmental activists – to come to a compromised position.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I believe all the clarification questions have been addressed.      .
